payload.summary: Planned contract-derived gen-eval descriptors. Root cause across three defects is that gen-eval has no notion of an operation: surface-local interface strings, hand-authored, with no link to the contract. Selected the contract-as-source model with generated, drift-guarded descriptors and reverse subset verifiers. Tier: coordinated; 6 work packages.

decisions.title: Contract is the source; introspection is the verifier
decisions.rationale: Direction is the whole design. If introspection populates the declared set, a broken or unreachable surface yields an empty set and unevaluated_interfaces == [] reports full coverage. PR #277 hit that class three times (UP-1 broken console script, UP-3 zero-scenario run, UP-4 health check that had to succeed). This INVERTS the existing normative statement in Requirement: Interface Descriptor, which currently mandates auto-discovery from tools/list and --help.

decisions.title: Every drift guard fails closed
decisions.rationale: A byte-diff alone is satisfied by 'empty == empty' — both files can rot to nothing together and stay green. Guards assert non-emptiness and an operation-count match against the contract before diffing.

decisions.title: Coverage keyed on operation x surface, with exposure first-class
decisions.rationale: The coordinator's 38 HTTP / 39 MCP / 37 CLI counts prove surfaces are genuinely partial, so 'not exposed on surface X' must be first-class or every derived descriptor carries permanent false gaps. Also fixes one operation tested once counting as two remaining gaps.

decisions.title: Tool contracts get their own schema rather than reusing OpenAPI
decisions.rationale: OpenAPI cannot express exit codes, and a tool's flags are process configuration rather than operation parameters. Forcing --fail-threshold into an OpenAPI operation would be the same category error UP-4 corrected in the lifecycle.

next_steps: Start with wp-contracts - it is the DAG root and every other package validates against cli-contract.schema.json.
wp-tool-descriptor and wp-service-descriptor then run in parallel on disjoint write scopes (descriptor.py vs service_descriptor.py).
Acceptance signal for wp-integration: `make dogfood` must stop reporting '0 interfaces'.
